messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High 5xx rate detected for inference-usw2a (az1a). Symptoms: resolver timeouts + per-host RX drops. Alert: alert-az1a-resolver-4623459999. Pager: @jamie
jamie: ack, looking now :eyes:
sasha: i'll pull net metrics and kernel logs on the affected hosts, grabbing tcpdump if necessary
jamie: confirm NLB target 10.0.12.0/24 returning 502s, several g5 nodes with kernel rx_drop counter climbing
marc: seeing K/V cache eviction spikes and gRPC stream resets in the runtime logs, likely downstream network issues, not model code
alice: heads-up: platform-status draft ready, suggest short message: "Partial degradation in us-west-2a affecting inference latency/errors; routing mitigation in progress". want to post after mitigation decision
jamie: plan: 1) divert new traffic from az1a to az1b/usw2b 2) evacuate ephemeral instances in az1a 3) enable cross-region fallback if capacity needed. executing step 1 now
sasha: running quick checks: `for h in $(cat hosts_az1a); do ssh $h "cat /proc/net/dev | grep eth0"; done` - rx errors on ~40% of hosts
marc: can we try forcing resolver to 8.8.8.8 on a test host to validate DNS path? open to short experiment :thinking_face:
jamie: running a controlled resolver change on staging proxies first, will report results in ~2m
(t+2m) jamie: staging proxy test -> successful, upstream resolver fallback to 8.8.8.8 clears timeouts for that proxy :thumbsup:
sasha: kernel trace shows bursts of rx queue processing latency around 22:14 UTC, likely network fabric hiccup. filing a cloud provider support ticket now
marc: starting graceful drain of targets in az1a for the inference NLB. command:
```
./infra/drain-az.sh --az az1a --service inference-nlb --mode graceful
```
jamie: initiated traffic shift to az1b/usw2b, autoscaling policy temporarily increased to handle extra load :shipit:
alice: posting status update now: "Investigating elevated errors for inference in us-west-2a. Traffic being rerouted; mitigation in progress. We'll update in 30m or sooner." link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/4623459999 :loudspeaker:
taylor: product teams - any high-priority customers to call out? we should prepare targeted comms if they are affected
jamie: Eng-sre to run targeted checks for top 10 customers. sasha, can you take lead on customer impact matrix?
sasha: on it, compiling list and brief impact levels now
incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-3147 | Severity: P1 | Owner: jamie | Runbook: https://runbooks/redwood/az-network-deg
jamie: cloud support responded: investigating TOR-level interface saturations in az1a, ETA unknown. recommend keep traffic shifted and avoid redeploys to az1a for now
marc: enabling KV cache warmup in az1b to reduce cold-start errors during traffic shift. command: `./runtime/cache-warmup --cluster inference-usw2b`
alice: posted customer-facing note to status and sent draft to comms channel. will hold for final approval before email blast
jamie: short term mitigation successful: error rate dropped ~80% after traffic shift. continuing monitoring. keeping incident open for oncall handoff
sasha: compiled customer impact doc and slack thread summary, adding CPU/memory error charts to the ticket
jamie: handing off primary oncall to @sasha for next 2h while i take PM coordination. add any escalations to this thread. :white_check_mark:
sasha: taking over. will keep watch and coordinate with cloud support. if rx drops persist after 30m of cloud fix attempts, we'll consider cross-region scale-up
marc: leaving a note: postmortem scope will include: resolver failover behaviour, NLB target health thresholds, runbook timing. tagging infra and runtime teams
alice: nice work team. filing post-incident comm plan and scheduling postmortem 24-48h. :calendar:
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-3147 status updated: mitigated -> partial; action required: postmortem + provider RCA.
jamie: closing my active pager. all further ops under @sasha. thanks everyone :pray:
